From 8f993d30b95dc9557a8a96ceca11abed674c8acb Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 11:02:54 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] usb: gadget: f_ncm: validate minimum block_len in
 ncm_unwrap_ntb()

The block_len read from the host-supplied NTB header is checked against
ntb_max but has no lower bound. When block_len is smaller than
opts->ndp_size, the bounds check of:
	ndp_index > (block_len - opts->ndp_size)
will underflow producing a huge unsigned value that ndp_index can never
exceed, defeating the check entirely.

The same underflow occurs in the datagram index checks against block_len
- opts->dpe_size.  With those checks neutered, a malicious USB host can
choose ndp_index and datagram offsets that point past the actual
transfer, and the skb_put_data() copies adjacent kernel memory into the
network skb.

Fix this by rejecting block lengths that cannot hold at least the NTB
header plus one NDP.  This will make block_len - opts->ndp_size and
block_len - opts->dpe_size both well-defined.

Commit 8d2b1a1ec9f5 ("CDC-NCM: avoid overflow in sanity checking") fixed
a related class of issues on the host side of NCM.

Fixes: 2b74b0a04d3e ("USB: gadget: f_ncm: add bounds checks to ncm_unwrap_ntb()")
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Assisted-by: gregkh_clanker_t1000
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/2026040753-baffle-handheld-624d@gregkh
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/usb/gadget/function/f_ncm.c b/drivers/usb/gadget/function/f_ncm.c
index a6fa5ed3d6cb..c5bf8a448d64 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/gadget/function/f_ncm.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/gadget/function/f_ncm.c
@@ -1210,8 +1210,8 @@ static int ncm_unwrap_ntb(struct gether *port,
 
 	block_len = get_ncm(&tmp, opts->block_length);
 	/* (d)wBlockLength */
-	if (block_len > ntb_max) {
-		INFO(port->func.config->cdev, "OUT size exceeded\n");
+	if ((block_len < opts->nth_size + opts->ndp_size) || (block_len > ntb_max)) {
+		INFO(port->func.config->cdev, "Bad block length: %#X\n", block_len);
 		goto err;
 	}
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch Modifications

This patch fixes a vulnerability in the USB gadget f_ncm driver by adding a lower bound check for the `block_len` value parsed from an NTB header.

### File Modified and Change

**File:** `drivers/usb/gadget/function/f_ncm.c`

- **Function:** `ncm_unwrap_ntb()`
- **Change:** The existing bounds check on `block_len` (line 1213) was expanded from:
  ```c
  if (block_len > ntb_max)
  ```
  to:
  ```c
  if ((block_len < opts->nth_size + opts->ndp_size) || (block_len > ntb_max))
  ```
  This ensures that `block_len` is both **at least** the minimum size required to hold an NTB header plus one NDP (Network Data Pointer) and **at most** `ntb_max`.

### Relationships Within the Change

- The addition of the lower bound prevents arithmetic underflow in two subsequent checks:
  - `ndp_index > (block_len - opts->ndp_size)` – when `block_len` is smaller than `opts->ndp_size`, the subtraction yields a huge unsigned value, bypassing the intended bounds check.
  - Datagram index checks against `block_len - opts->dpe_size` – similarly vulnerable to underflow.
- By requiring `block_len >= opts->nth_size + opts->ndp_size`, both subtractions become safe (well-defined non-negative results), restoring the effectiveness of the security checks that were added in commit 2b74b0a04d3e.
- This fix prevents a malicious USB host from supplying a crafted `block_len` that bypasses bounds checks and allows reading adjacent kernel memory into a network packet via `skb_put_data()`.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (block_len > ntb_max) {
```
and the underflow‑vulnerable bounds checks:
```c
(ndp_index > (block_len - opts->ndp_size))
(index > block_len - opts->dpe_size)
```

Reason:  
The `block_len` value from the NTB header was only checked against an upper limit (`ntb_max`). When `block_len` is smaller than `opts->ndp_size` (or `opts->dpe_size`), the subtractions `block_len - opts->ndp_size` and `block_len - opts->dpe_size` wrap around to a very large unsigned number. Consequently the comparisons `ndp_index > (block_len - opts->ndp_size)` and `index > block_len - opts->dpe_size` always evaluate to false, bypassing the intended bounds checks. This allows a malicious host to supply `ndp_index` and datagram offsets that point past the actual transfer buffer, causing `skb_put_data()` to copy adjacent kernel memory into the network skb.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if ((block_len < opts->nth_size + opts->ndp_size) || (block_len > ntb_max)) {
```

Reason:  
The new condition adds a lower bound check requiring `block_len` to be at least as large as the NTB header (`nth_size`) plus one NDP (`ndp_size`). This ensures that both `block_len - opts->ndp_size` and `block_len - opts->dpe_size` are well‑defined (non‑negative) in subsequent arithmetic, preventing unsigned underflow. With valid subtraction results, the existing bounds checks for `ndp_index` and datagram indices work correctly, blocking out‑of‑range offsets.
